perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: revenueMixQuality
factors.basis: Serve's August 6 Q2 release said higher-margin recurring revenue rose to more than 50% of total revenue and gross margin improved sequentially.

risks: Improving mix does not establish positive gross profit dollars, operating leverage or fleet-level profitability.
contradictions: Revenue mix and gross margin improved while the company remains in a high-investment scaling phase and mix quality alone does not prove durable unit economics.
unknowns: Absolute recurring-revenue dollars, contribution margin by vertical and revenue per robot were not disclosed in the headline release.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: liquidityAndDiversification
factors.basis: Serve ended Q2 with more than $240 million in cash and marketable securities and reported triple-digit growth across delivery, branding and software, while adding laundry alongside food, healthcare and grocery delivery.

risks: Liquidity supports execution runway but does not prove that diversified pilots convert into profitable utilization.
unknowns: Cash burn trajectory and incremental economics of newer verticals remain key underwriting unknowns.

sources.origin: Serve Robotics Investor Relations / Q2 2026 results
facts: Serve reported more than 400% year-over-year Q2 revenue growth.
Higher-margin recurring revenue exceeded 50% of total revenue and gross margin improved sequentially.
Serve ended Q2 with more than $240 million in cash and marketable securities.
Revenue applications included food, healthcare, grocery and a new laundry partnership.

result: Primary-source Q2 revenue-mix, liquidity and diversification evidence packaged for Alpha; numeric underwriting remains Alpha-owned.
